items.title: 6.3.1 Standard Equation of the Parabola (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 183-184: 6.3.1 derivation of y^2 = 4ax with Figure 6.11.

blocks.text: Ab hum parabola ki equation banayenge. Tareeqa wohi hai jo locus ke har sawal mein hota hai: ek general point \(P(x, y)\) lo, us par definition wali shart lagao, aur phir simplify karo. Lekin pehle axes ko aqalmandi se rakhna hai taake equation sab se chhoti aaye.

Maan lijiye \(F\) parabola ka focus hai aur \(CD\) us ki directrix. Focus \(F\) se directrix \(CD\) par perpendicular \(FZ\) kheenchiye. \(V\) ko \(FZ\) ka mid-point lijiye aur \(FZ = 2a\) maan lijiye. \(V\) ko origin banaiye, \(x\)-axis line \(ZF\) ke saath saath, aur \(y\)-axis \(V\) par \(VF\) ke perpendicular, jaisa figure mein dikhaya gaya hai.

blocks.alt: Axes X prime X and Y prime Y meet at the vertex V. The vertical directrix CD cuts the x-axis at Z, to the left of V; the focus F is to the right of V with ZV = VF. A parabola opens to the right through V. A point P(x, y) on it is joined to F, and PM is drawn perpendicular to the directrix.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.11: Focus F, directrix CD and a point P of the parabola (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Axes aise kyun? Axes hum jahan chahein rakh sakte hain; hum unhein aise rakhte hain ke equation sab se saada bane. Vertex \(V\) ko origin aur \(x\)-axis ko focus se guzarne wali line banaya, to focus \((a, 0)\) ban gaya aur directrix vertical line \(x = -a\). Yahan \(a > 0\) vertex se focus tak ka faasla hai, aur utna hi vertex se directrix tak. Yaani \(FZ = 2a\) ko \(V\) ne beech se do barabar hisson \(a\) aur \(a\) mein baant diya.
\(V\) focus aur directrix dono se barabar door hai (dono taraf \(a\)), is liye definition ke mutabiq \(V\) khud parabola par hai. Is point \(V\) ko parabola ka vertex kehte hain.
Is tarah focus \(F(a, 0)\) aur directrix \(x = -a\) hai.

Ab asal kaam shuru hota hai. Hum parabola par koi bhi point \(P(x, y)\) le rahe hain; 'koi bhi' ka matlab hai ke jo equation banegi woh har point par lagu hogi. Is point ke do faasle nikalne hain: ek focus tak aur ek directrix tak. Phir definition ke mutabiq dono ko barabar rakhenge.

Ab parabola par koi bhi point \(P(x, y)\) lijiye aur \(CD\) par perpendicular \(PM\) kheenchiye. Focus se faasla distance formula se:
\[|PF| = \sqrt{(x-a)^{2} + (y-0)^{2}}\]
\[= \sqrt{x^{2} - 2ax + a^{2} + y^{2}}\]
Directrix \(x = -a\) se \(P\) ka faasla:
\[|PM| = \dfrac{|x + a|}{\sqrt{1^{2} + 0^{2}}} = |x + a|\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yahan do mukhtalif faasle ke formulas lage hain.
\(|PF|\): do points \((x, y)\) aur \((a, 0)\) ke darmiyan distance formula.
\(|PM|\): point se line tak faasla. Directrix ko \(x + a = 0\) likhein, yaani \(1\cdot x + 0\cdot y + a = 0\); to faasla \(\frac{|x + a|}{\sqrt{1^{2} + 0^{2}}}\) aata hai. Aasaan nazar se dekhein to \(M\) ka \(y\) wohi hai jo \(P\) ka hai, is liye yeh sirf \(x\) aur \(-a\) ka horizontal farq hai, jaise ruler se seedha naap lena.

Ab definition lagayein: \(|PF| = |PM|\). Is liye
\[\sqrt{x^{2} - 2ax + a^{2} + y^{2}} = |x + a|\]
Dono taraf square karne se
\[x^{2} - 2ax + a^{2} + y^{2} = (x + a)^{2}\]
\[x^{2} - 2ax + a^{2} + y^{2} = x^{2} + 2ax + a^{2}\]
aur simplify karne par
Yeh parabola ki standard equation hai.

Ruk kar dekhiye hum ne kya kiya. Shuru mein sirf ek shart thi (do faasle barabar), aur aakhir mein ek chhoti si equation mil gayi. Yahi coordinate geometry ki taaqat hai: geometry ki baat ko algebra ki equation mein badal dena. Ab jab bhi koi point \(y^{2} = 4ax\) ko satisfy kare, hum yaqeen se keh sakte hain ke woh focus aur directrix se barabar door hai, aur ulta bhi.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Jo chhota qadam kitab ne chhor diya: dono taraf se \(x^{2}\) aur \(a^{2}\) cancel karein:
\[-2ax + y^{2} = 2ax\]
\[y^{2} = 4ax\]
Square karna yahan theek kyun hai? Dono taraf faasle hain, is liye dono \(\ge 0\) hain; aur do non-negative numbers tab hi barabar hote hain jab un ke squares barabar hon. Saath hi \(|x + a|^{2} = (x + a)^{2}\), is liye modulus (absolute value ka nishan) khud hi khatam ho gaya.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Equation \(y^{2} = 4ax\) (\(a > 0\)) se kya pata chalta hai?
\(y^{2}\) kabhi negative nahi hota, is liye \(x \ge 0\) hona chahiye: poora curve \(y\)-axis ke daayen taraf hai, yaani focus ki taraf khulta hai aur directrix se door.
\(y\) ki jagah \(-y\) rakhne se equation nahi badalti, is liye curve \(x\)-axis ke upar aur neeche bilkul ek jaisa (symmetric) hai, jaise aaine mein aks.
Misaal: \(a = 1\) ho to \(y^{2} = 4x\) points \((0, 0)\), \((1, \pm 2)\), \((4, \pm 4)\) se guzarta hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Upar wale curve \(y^{2} = 4x\) par point \((4, 4)\) lein. Focus \((1, 0)\) se faasla \(\sqrt{9 + 16} = 5\), aur directrix \(x = -1\) se faasla \(4 + 1 = 5\). Barabar! Ab aap point \((9, 6)\) ke saath khud yahi check kijiye (jawab: dono faasle 10).

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text: Focus \((2, 0)\) aur directrix \(x = -2\) wale parabola ki equation kya hogi? Yahan vertex origin par hai aur \(a = 2\), is liye \(y^{2} = 4(2)x = 8x\). Ab definition se khud tasdeeq kijiye: \((x - 2)^{2} + y^{2} = (x + 2)^{2}\) ko khol kar dekhein, \(x^{2}\) aur 4 cancel ho kar \(y^{2} = 8x\) hi bachta hai. Yaani formula aur definition ek hi jawab dete hain.

Ek mashwara: is derivation ko kam az kam ek baar khud kaghaz par bina dekhe likhiye. Exam mein 'derive the standard equation of parabola' aksar poocha jata hai, aur poore marks tab milte hain jab figure, axes ka intikhab, dono faasle, square karna aur aakhri simplification sab saaf likhe hon.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Axes ka intikhab: vertex origin par, \(x\)-axis focus se guzarta hua.
2. Phir focus \(F(a, 0)\), directrix \(x = -a\), vertex \(V(0, 0)\), aur \(a\) = vertex se focus ka faasla.
3. Standard equation: \(y^{2} = 4ax\).
4. Derivation ek line mein: \(|PF| = |PM|\), square, cancel.
5. Curve daayen taraf khulta hai aur \(x\)-axis ke gird symmetric hai.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(a\) ko focus se directrix tak ka faasla samajhna. Woh faasla \(2a\) hai; \(a\) us ka aadha hai.
2. \(|PM| = x - a\) likh dena. Directrix \(x = -a\) hai, is liye \(|PM| = |x - (-a)| = |x + a|\).
3. \((x + a)^{2}\) ko \(x^{2} + a^{2}\) likh kar beech wala term \(2ax\) bhool jana.
